translation_source: Samuel Butler, 1900. Project Gutenberg #1727 (source-texts/pg1727-butler-1900.txt). The only translation used; no other consulted for wording (Fagles, Lattimore, Wilson, Fitzgerald not read).

source_verification.method: Independent reconstruction of PG #1727 lines 741-1116, written to a rule devised for this Book and audited against the raw lines before being trusted, then diffed against the staged original-en. NOT a re-run of whatever produced the served file.
source_verification.rule: The translation body contains exactly 187 digit runs and, read in order, they are the sequence 1..187 with no repeats and no gaps, against 186 bracketed entries in PG's FOOTNOTES: list numbered to 187 (only 29 absent, and that gap is in Book III). The counts reconcile, so every digit run in the body is a footnote reference and Butler's body carries no digits of its own. The rule is applied POSITIONALLY - the k-th run removed must BE the k-th marker - so a stray body digit breaks the arithmetic instead of vanishing, which a pattern rule ('delete any digit run') would not catch.
source_verification.result: 35 of 35 paragraphs byte-identical, zero diffs; 4184 words compared word-for-word.
source_verification.audit: PG lines 741-1116: 0 indented lines, 0 [Illustration markers, 0 in-text Greek, 0 daggers, 0 underscores, 1 square bracket (Butler's own '[do not]' at line 802, kept by the staged file), 7 footnote markers (17-23) on 6 lines, 11 short standalone lines all verified paragraph-final. Two audit catches recorded: 'FOOTNOTES:' occurs twice in the file and the first (line 75) is the table of contents - anchoring on it makes the body empty and the relation vacuously true; and Book 2's markers are never preceded by a space, so the rule's whitespace clause is a no-op here.
source_verification.negative_controls: Joining a paragraph's lines with a space instead of a newline differs in 35 of 35 paragraphs; leaving the markers in differs in 5 of 35. The check is capable of failing.

word_counts.note: Screening signal only; not evidence of semantic completeness, in either direction. Book 2 sits far closer to 1.0 than Book 1 (0.9462) because it is a Book of speeches in plain argument with much less of the long Victorian sentence-chaining Book 1's narration carries. THE RATIO IS SUPERSEDED AS THE PRIMARY SIGNAL by the retention measure the round-1 reviewer introduced: the fraction of Butler's word tokens the candidate carries over unchanged AND in order (name mapping normalized, punctuation and case stripped, difflib matching blocks over word tokens; computed by scripts/build_book02_v2.py's token_retention()). It says what the ratio cannot - Book 2 is a substantially lighter rewrite than accepted Book 1 (0.889 against 0.721) at a near-identical word ratio. The reviewer then read the paragraphs it points at and ruled the lightness is the source's, not the drafter's: the least-changed paragraphs are plain dialogue and plain concrete narration where Butler is already modern English. Its one catch is finding 26.1, in the Book's HIGHEST-retention paragraph. The two counter-checks v1 offered - no paragraph byte-identical to Butler, and 22 dead words gone - are retained as floors but are weak: a rewrite changing one word per paragraph satisfies both. Retention rose from v1 to v2 because 19 of the 23 corrections put a word of Butler's back; a round that moved it down would be a warning.

punctuation.standard: PUNCTUATION.md: typographic quotation marks and apostrophes throughout. Verified: zero ASCII apostrophes and zero ASCII double quotes in the candidate.
punctuation.quotation_balance: candidate 29 open / 28 close, identical to the source's 29 / 28.
punctuation.d4_preserved: Butler's unclosed quotation at B02-P006 into B02-P007 (Antinous's continuous speech) is reproduced exactly; it is the only unbalanced paragraph in either file. The inner single quotation round Penelope's own speech IS closed at B02-P006's end, which is Butler and not a slip.

base_text_defects: One. B02-P004 carries Butler's own square bracket, '[do not] hold back' (PG #1727 line 802), which the staged original-en keeps verbatim. It is Butler's bracket, not PG apparatus. The candidate drops the mark and keeps the words, with a colon introduced to carry the pointing. RULED AT ROUND 1: the disposition is upheld and the reason v1 recorded for it was wrong. It is NOT a textual mark. Butler's footnote 18, attached to this sentence (PG line 10926, verified directly), reads: 'The authoress has bungled by borrowing these words verbatim from the Iliad, without prefixing the necessary "do not," which I have supplied.' So it is a translator's supplement, supplied against the Greek, flagged as supplied and defended in a note - which makes keeping the words Butler's judgement and not this package's, since he calls them necessary. Now decision D12, CLASS A, and the poem's only class-A bracket. D12 is written by class because Butler brackets at least three different things: class B (unflagged explanatory supplement inside the line - same disposition, weaker warrant, flagged per instance; Book 3 meets the first at PG 1129, '[on the embers]') and class C (a passage Butler brackets as an afterthought or interpolation; first at PG 1551 in Book 4, footnote 36) - and class C is OPEN and blocks Book 4, because dropping the mark there silently converts recorded editorial doubt into narration. All fifteen brackets in the translation body are enumerated in GLOSSARY.md. See continuity.md 'Base-text defects'.
glosses: One, at B02-P008: 'the Erinyes-the spirits of vengeance-to avenge her'. Three words at first use, folded into the sentence, on the Book 10 pilot's 'cubit -> roughly eighteen inches' model. The English alternative 'the Furies' is a Roman name and is not available to this edition.

review_round_1: Complete. review/findings-v1.md, independent reviewer session spawned by the coordinator, on candidate-v1.json. Verdict: Accept after corrections - 0 substantive, 16 minor (14 paragraph-level + 2 records), 11 optional by the reviewer's summary table and 10 by its own numbered entries (8 paragraph-level + 2 records), 19 paragraphs with no material issue. Coverage: every ID B02-P001..B02-P035 exactly once. Every finding answered; every one applied; none declined. The reviewer re-verified the source on a different KIND of rule from the drafter's - identifying nothing in advance, diffing with PG's apparatus still in, and classifying every difference before removing anything: 7 differences in 5 paragraphs, all bare footnote-marker digit runs, then 35 of 35 byte-identical. It also introduced the Butler-token retention measure now recorded in word_counts. No second round requested or required.
